scope: Frontend credential storage, API client, session management, page reload, concurrent requests

evidence.observation: Access token is stored in a module-level variable that is not persisted to any storage mechanism (localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies). On page refresh, this variable resets to null, losing the token.
logout() redirects to /login page via window.location.href. The logout API call is fire-and-forget with no error handling or guarantee of completion before redirect.

When 401 is received, the client attempts to refresh the session. If refresh fails, it calls logout() which redirects to login page and throws an error. However, if multiple concurrent requests all receive 401 simultaneously, all will attempt refresh concurrently.
refreshSession() has no locking mechanism or deduplication. Multiple concurrent requests with 401 will all call refreshSession() independently, creating a race condition.

Dashboard makes 3 concurrent API calls on mount with no error boundary or catch handler. If one call fails, Promise.all rejects and state is not updated. No error handling means silent failure or redirect to login without visual indication.

Token is retrieved at the time of the request. On page refresh, _accessToken is null, so no Authorization header is sent with the initial request. The request is made with credentials but without a token.
After login, the token is set and then the page is redirected. If navigation happens before the token is fully set in application state, a race condition can occur.

hypotheses.statement: On page refresh, the access token stored in _accessToken is lost because it is only stored in memory (not persisted to localStorage, sessionStorage, or cookies). When the page reloads, the module reinitializes and _accessToken becomes null. Subsequent API requests are sent without an Authorization header, causing 401 responses.

When multiple concurrent API requests are made (e.g., the three calls in Dashboard.useEffect), and the token has expired, all three requests receive 401 and all three concurrently call refreshSession() without coordination. This creates a race condition where the token may be overwritten multiple times or refreshSession may fail due to rate limiting or backend state issues.

When logout() is called (triggered by a failed refresh after 401), it performs an async fetch to /auth/logout but does not await it. The fire-and-forget pattern means window.location.href = '/login' executes immediately, potentially before the logout API call completes, leaving the backend session in an inconsistent state.

Dashboard.useEffect makes three concurrent API calls without error handling (no .catch() or error boundary). When all three requests fail due to an expired token, Promise.all rejects, the catch block is missing, and the logout() redirect is triggered silently without any user-facing error message, creating the appearance of a random logout.

If the refresh token (stored in httpOnly cookie via credentials: 'include') is also expired or invalid, refreshSession() returns false immediately. The client calls logout(), which redirects to /login. This happens silently from the user's perspective because the only error is thrown but never caught in Dashboard.
